memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If a man marries his brother's wife, it is an act of impurity; he has dishonoured his brother. They will be childless.'" - Lev 20:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This law had consequences no one at Sinai could have foreseen.

Fifteen centuries later, a preacher in the wilderness confronted a king. Herod Antipas had taken his brother's wife, Herodias, and John the Baptist told him plainly: it is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife (Mark 6:18).

It cost John his life. Herodias nursed a grudge, waited for her moment at a birthday feast, and John was beheaded in a prison cell.

Think about what John could have done instead. He could have stayed silent. Herod was a dangerous man, and John was not obliged to seek him out. He could have reasoned that a prophet's ministry is worth more alive than dead.

But John spoke, because God's word applied to kings as much as to peasants.

That is a costly kind of faithfulness, and it is not always ours to choose. Not every situation calls for confrontation, and wisdom matters. But there are moments when silence would be easier and truth needs saying — and God's people have generally been at their best when they did not calculate the cost first.

Jesus said of John: among those born of women there has not risen anyone greater (Matt 11:11).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has fear of consequences kept you silent?
2. How do you tell the difference between wisdom and cowardice?
3. What truth might God be asking you to speak this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me courage to speak truth when it costs me, and wisdom to know when and how. Make me faithful rather than merely comfortable. Amen.
